result.title: Continual Learning for Reliable In-Sequence Molecular Communication
result.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Published in 2026 20th IIAI International Congress on Advanced Applied Informatics
result.summary: This paper considers reliable in-sequence molecular communication, where bio-nanomachines exchange molecule-encoded information in a specified order, and investigates a new simulation-based method to incrementally evaluate communication protocols by gradually increasing the complexity of experimental settings. The proposed method, called Affine Memory Replay (AMR), builds a continual learning (CL) model to estimate communication performance between bio-nanomachines. AMR stores past simulation samples and synthesizes additional replay samples through interpolation and extrapolation between past samples. Through incremental performance estimation tasks, it replays both past and synthetic samples to regularize model updates, helping the model adapt to new experimental settings while retaining knowledge from earlier ones. Experimental results show that AMR significantly outperforms existing CL methods in maintaining overall estimation accuracy across sequentially learned estimation tasks. It effectively balances memory stability and learning plasticity under moderate training cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究分子通信中可靠的按序信息传递，提出 Affine Memory Replay：保存过去仿真样本并用插值、外推合成回放样本，在持续学习中正则化模型更新，以增量方式估计不同实验设置下的通信性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 领域与 LVR 相距较远，但其「回放旧样本＋插值/外推合成样本以平衡稳定性与可塑性」的持续学习思路，可供核查是否可用于 latent 推理轨迹的顺序训练与遗忘抑制。
